candidate: Model licence and gating preflight (kit-native practice, no version)
what: Before a base model, teacher model or downloaded adapter is first used, record repository id, revision, licence id, licence name and link, gated status, where each fact was read and the date; map the licence id to allow, ask or deny from a user-editable list.
problem_here: finetuning.md and resume.md pin the base revision but never ask what the licence allows; current small open-weight models range from Apache-2.0 and MIT to revenue thresholds, service clauses, naming duties and gated custom licences.
mechanism: Standard-library reader of model-card front matter and LICENSE files in a local model folder or cache snapshot; optional, off by default, GET of https://huggingface.co/api/models/REPO reading sha, gated, cardData.license, license_name, license_link; other, unknown, missing or gated gives ask; the agent never accepts a gate.
evidence: Hub API responses and licence texts read 2026-11-11 by this scout: Qwen3.5-4B apache-2.0; gemma-3-4b-it gated manual; Mistral Large 4 license other with a service clause; LFM Open License v1.0 USD 10M threshold; Muse Spark Open gated manual with a personal-data form; Llama 3.3 naming duty. No study measures the benefit.
maturity: New practice; licence ids and card fields documented at https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/repositories-licenses
cost: Small parser plus one policy list; the optional lookup is one HTTPS request that reveals the model name to the hub; hub labels can be wrong, so the verdict is a record, not legal clearance.
simpler_alternative: One Project-card line: base model licence, where it was read, who checked.
reason: Cheap, offline-capable, answers question 5 directly; the network lookup stays optional.
cheap_local_trial: Run the reader on one model folder that has a README with a license field and one that has none; expect the id for the first and ask for the second.

candidate: Tokenizer and chat-template preflight (render-and-decode check, kit-native practice)
what: Before any long language-model run: render three training examples, tokenise them the way the trainer does, and record BOS count, last token, end-of-sequence id list including generation_config, pad id and side, the decoded text of tokens that carry loss, truncated-example count and packing strategy.
problem_here: finetuning.md section 3 has five lines; current docs and 2026 release notes describe about fifteen separate silent failure points.
mechanism: A checklist with one source per item in the references, plus a short snippet the agent runs inside the project's own training environment; the kit only stores the output with the run. The standard library cannot render Jinja templates, so the kit itself imports nothing.
evidence: Transformers chat-templating guide v5.19.0 and TRL docs and release notes v1.14.0-v1.17.1 (EOS not appended, end-of-turn ids only in generation config, reasoning dropped by inference templates, wrapped packing duplicating data), read 2026-11-11; measured by the library maintainers as bug reports, not as a controlled study.
maturity: Practice assembled from official docs; no release.
cost: A few minutes per project; the snippet depends on the project's tokenizer library; risk of false comfort if only short examples are rendered.
simpler_alternative: Keep the existing instruction to inspect 5 rendered examples.
reason: Highest-value language-model addition; advice text in core, executable part runs in the project environment.
cheap_local_trial: In an environment with transformers, render one chat example for a small cached model and print token ids, label mask and eos ids; takes under a minute.

candidate: Frozen generation settings in the evaluation contract (kit-native practice)
what: Treat decoding parameters, chat template, stop ids, maximum new tokens, seed, inference engine, engine version and hardware as part of the frozen evaluator for any score computed from generated text.
problem_here: The kit freezes the evaluator files but not the settings that live in model repositories or engine defaults; a model swap can silently switch sampling on.
mechanism: A generation block recorded with final_eval_commands and compared between runs; mismatch means scores are not comparable.
evidence: Gemma 4 generation_config.json enables sampling (temperature 1.0, top-k 64, top-p 0.95) and lists three eos ids; vLLM docs (8 Oct 2026) say results are not reproducible by default and only on the same hardware and version; transformers docs say generate returns at most 20 new tokens by default. Read 2026-11-11.
maturity: Practice; lm-evaluation-harness already saves the chat template with results.
cost: A few config fields and one comparison; no dependency.
simpler_alternative: The current sentence in finetuning.md: record decoding parameters.
reason: Validity is the top-ranked quality attribute and this is a known source of false gains.
cheap_local_trial: Generate from one small cached model twice with repository defaults and twice with do_sample false; compare outputs.

what: After merging, quantising or converting a model, run the frozen evaluator on the exported artefact with its embedded template before reporting any number for it.

mechanism: A reference rule plus one journal field: artefact evaluated, format, tool and version.
evidence: PEFT docs: merging with torchao is only correct for LoRA with int8_weight_only; llama.cpp keeps separate conversion scripts; vendor research reports hidden instructions in GGUF templates (search summary only). Read 2026-11-11. No measured effect size.
cost: One extra evaluation per export.
simpler_alternative: Report only pre-export scores and say so.
reason: Cheap and closes a real gap between what was evaluated and what is shipped.
cheap_local_trial: none (needs an export tool; with llama.cpp installed in WSL2 it takes minutes for a sub-1B model)

candidate: Untrusted model code and weight-format rule (kit-native practice)

mechanism: Reference rule plus an optional guard check that flags trust_remote_code=True in a launched script or auto_map in a model config.json.
evidence: Vendor research published 29 Oct 2026: 31 malicious hub repositories executed through trust_remote_code and auto_map, scanners returned clean results; Hugging Face pickle page says its scanner is not foolproof. Read 2026-11-11.
maturity: Practice; safetensors is the hub's own recommended format.
cost: Some legitimate models need remote code and will need an approval step; a text match can be evaded.

cheap_local_trial: Search a sample training script and a cached config.json for the two markers with a plain text search.
